title: Black community jazz festivals, labels like Be-bop, and lineage
summary: He argues for incubators for jazz in black communities and criticizes writers' labels.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x:
For example, Dan, I'm in a peculiar position now. I've always been interested in trying to stimulate local interest in activities like Jazz Festival Society in Chicago---in Philadelphia, and I organized the New York Jazz Festival Society here. I haven't done anything important with it. But I think that, why can't mainstreams and guys who know the history of jazz, why can't we begin to build in black communities this kind of thing where incubators are created and out of that can evolve more of the original kind of things that's needed."
But sometimes I blame writers, you know what I mean, guys--I'm not calling any names 'cause they know who they are--who would create a term like Be-bop, Swing, Jazz, Honky-tonk, etc., etc., etc. All of these came out of a certain basic pattern. And no matter be it Charlie Parker...I played a concert with
Charlie Parker and he said to me, 'Sam, you just play what you play and I'll play what I play and it'll come out all right.'

So, at 71, having played the piano 58 years, you know what I mean, I feel like that I have something to say or something to contribute, and that it should be put down and it should not be...the fact that I played for thirty years and for ten years nobody heard of me. That's what happened with Bunk Johnson...that's a cardinal example. They didn't hear from him 'cause he didn't have any teeth. They didn't hear from him because he was on a rice field.

Where was the lineage? Where was the direct line so that you could see, Dan...where...what happened in 1908, '09, '10, '11, '12, '13, '14, '15 should not be a break in the history of blacks in jazz. I say this, and I say it quite candidly, that I've been very, very disturbed that Duke Ellington died several years ago...do they play his music? Yes. And I'm sure they get the royalties. I'm sure that he was astute enough to have that kind of arrangement, and lawyers and...to take care of that. But what about heritage? What about the roots? What about the tradition? What about the carrying it on? What about...do you see? What about his son living in Denmark, I'm told, and, /he inherited the band. Where's the band? Where's the incubator? Where are the new creators coming out of Duke's idiom? Where are the creators coming out of Louis Armstrong?
